methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $6.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, a Series D-stage climate and energy company, is valued at $6.0B post-money following $2.3B+ in cumulative capital raised. The relevant comp universe comprises nine peers—one public (LNZA) and eight private—operating in the same sector at similar or adjacent funding stages, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, and QuantumScape.

Two valuation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression applies a typical 1.5x multiplier from Series D to subsequent-stage funding, yielding $9.0B. Peer-median triangulation examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M, producing a median of $1.0B but acknowledging a wide range of $700M to $3.0B across the sample.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $850M (low) to $10.3B (high), with a median of $5.0B. The current $6.0B valuation sits near the midpoint of this range. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations—reflecting heterogeneity in technology maturity, capital efficiency, and market readiness within climate tech—and the limited applicability of public comps to private frontier-stage dynamics. The peer-median method, anchored to smaller-stage comparables, suggests material upside to the stage-progression method, warranting further scrutiny of relative execution risk and capital deployment efficiency.
